newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CEO Eaton's income tripled in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CEO Eaton's income tripled in 1996.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. Chairman Robert Eaton's total compensation more than tripled to $12.6 million as he cashed in on the company's strong performance in 1996, the company said Friday in its annual proxy statment.

Eaton's income included exercised stock options worth more than $4.4 million. In 1995, he earned a total of $4.1 million in salary, bonus and other compensation but did not exercise any stock options.

In a year in which Detroit's No. 3 automaker reported near-record net income, Eaton's 1996 salary, bonus and other compensation total of $8.2 million included a 91 percent increase in his bonus to $4.5 million from $2.36 million in 1995.

As the company released the proxy report, Chrysler suspended production at four light truck assembly plants in Michigan, St. Louis and Windsor, Ontario, because of an engine plant strike. More than 12,000 workers were idled.
The plants make the Dodge Ram and Dodge Dakota pickup trucks, Jeep Grand Cherokee sport utility vehicles and full-size vans.

About 1,800 members of UAW Local 51 struck Chrysler's Mound Road engine plant in Detroit early Thursday in a dispute over staffing levels and the proposed shifting of work to outside contractors at a cost of up to 300 jobs. The plant supplies engines for Chrysler's light truck products.
Chrysler said Eaton's base salary increased to $1.4 million from $1.2 million and he received $2 million under a long-term incentive plan, up from $434,981 in such payments in 1995.
The chairman's compensation does not include a grant for new, unexercised stock options for 696,018 shares, which were given a present value of $4.5 million.

Bolstered by strong truck, Jeep and minivan sales, Chrysler's 1996 net income reached a near-record $3.53 billion, up 74 percent over the $2.03 billion it earned in 1995, a year in which Chrysler experienced a costly launch of its current minivans.

Chrysler Vice Chairman Robert Lutz, who has agreed to stay at the automaker for about two years following his 65th birthday in February, also saw his total compensation, including exercised stock options, jump in 1996 to $10.8 million from $4 million in 1995.
Lutz exercised options worth $5.7 million in 1996, compared with $1.1 million in 1995. He also received new, unexercised options for 267,591 Chrysler shares, valued at $1.8 million.
As a group, Chrysler's top five executives earned a total of $21.1 million in salary, bonus and other compensation in 1996, up 79 percent from the $11.8 million they earned in 1995.
